THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE G BASAVARAJA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The appellant has preferred this appeal against the order dated 08.12.2025 passed in Crl.Misc.No.1200/2025 by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga (for short 'the trial Court').
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the trial Court.
NC: 2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR 3.

Brief facts leading to this appeal are that, on the basis of the complaint filed by victim,
Shivamogga Rural Police have registered the case in Crime No.357/2025 against the appellant/accused for the commission of offence under Sections 75(1)(i), 75(1)(ii), 351(2), 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(va), 3(2)(vii), 3(1)(w)(i) of the SC &
ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015.

sentences.text: The appellant had filed application under Section 482 of BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail.
Same came to be rejected by the trial Court.
Being aggrieved by rejection of application, the appellant has preferred this appeal.
5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant would submit that the impugned order is illegal, perverse and liable to be set aside.
The accused has not committed any offence as alleged against him.

The offence alleged to have been committed by the appellant are not for the reasons that respondent No.2 belongs to Scheduled NC: 2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR Caste/Scheduled Tribe.
Infact, she does not belong to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
The offence alleged against the accused are not exclusively punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
The trial Court has not taken into consideration the relevant circumstances and factors while passing the impugned order and dismissing the petition.
The accused is aged 51 years working as Assistant Sub-inspector of Police, a public servant and he is the only earning member of his family.
If he is arrested and committed to custody, there is every likelihood of losing employment.
The complainant had filed case against one Krishnamurthy K.H, was registered in SC.No.190/2014, in which accused was acquitted.
Neither the State nor the victim has preferred any appeal against the judgment passed by the III Additional Sessions Judge, Shivamogga in SC.No.190/2014.
The appellant is ready to abide by the conditions which may be imposed by this Court.
On all these grounds, it is sought to allow this appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR 6.

Learned counsel Smt. Parineeta S, appearing on behalf of respondent No.2 and Sri B.Lakshman,
learned HCGP appearing for the respondent-State, would submit that the trial court has properly appreciated the materials on record and sought for dismissal of this appeal.
7. I have examined the materials placed before this court.

On the basis of the complaint filed by victim, Shivamogga Rural Police have registered the case against the accused for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 75(1)(i), 75(1)(ii), 351(2), 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 and sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(va), 3(2)(vii), 3(1)(w)(i) of the SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015.

sentences.text: 9. In column No.3 of the FIR, the date of the commission of offence is stated commencing from 01.01.2025 to 26.11.2025.
The complaint came to be filed on 26.11.2025 and FIR was submitted to the court on 27.11.2025 at 10.40 am.
After lapse of more than ten months from the date of commission of offence, the complainant has lodged the complaint.

In column No.3(c) NC:
2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR of FIR, the Investigating Officer has not shown any reasons for delay in filing the complaint.
10. On plain reading of this complaint, at this stage, it is crystal clear that the appellant has not abused the complainant in presence of public.
Therefore, at this stage, there are no sufficient prima facie materials to constitute the penal provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989.
The copy of the judgment passed in SC.No.190/2014 filed by State by Mahila Police Station, Shivamogga reveals that the present complainant is shown as PW1.
She had filed a complaint against one Krishnamurthy K H @ Viveka.

On the basis of this complaint, case was registered and thereafter charge sheet was filed against the accused for the commission of offence under Sections 376(1) and 417 of IPC.
11.
On 14.08.2015, the III Additional Sessions Judge, Shivamogga has acquitted the accused for the offence under Sections 376 and 417 Indian Penal Code.
The State NC: 2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR or victim has not preferred any appeal against the judgment of acquittal passed by the III Additional Sessions Judge, Shivamogga.
Taking into consideration the inordinate delay in filing the complaint and previous antecedents of the appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case

,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed;
(ii) The order dated 08.12.2025 passed in Crl.Misc.No.1200/2025 by the II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Shivamogga, is set aside.

application filed under Section 482 of BNSS, 2023, is allowed, subject to following conditions:
a. Appellant/accused shall be released on bail on executing a self-bond of Rs.1,00,000/- with one surety for likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer in the event of his arrest in Crime No.357/2025 of Shivamogga Rural Police;
NC: 2026:KHC:5387 HC-KAR b.
Appellant/accused shall not tamper or threaten the prosecution witness in any manner;
